title: Principal localization of an associated module sheaf
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a ring homomorphism, let $M$ be a $B$-module,
and let $a\in A$. For the
associated quasi-coherent sheaf
$\widetilde M$ on $\operatorname{Spec}B$, restriction induces

$$
\Gamma\bigl(\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_AA_a),\widetilde M\bigr)
\cong M\otimes_AA_a.
$$

proof.text: Write $b$ for the image of $a$ in $B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], $B\otimes_A A_a$ is the localization of $B$ at the powers of $b$, hence its spectrum is the principal open $D(b)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$; the restriction of $\widetilde M$ to this open is therefore the sheaf appearing in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections].
Applying [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] with $R=B$, $N=M$, and $r=b$ gives $\Gamma(D(b),\widetilde M)\cong M_b$ via $m/b^n\mapsto b^{-n}m$.

The universal properties of the principal localization identify $B\otimes_A A_a$ with $B_b$ and identify the base-changed module $M\otimes_A A_a$ with $M_b$, by $m\otimes(x/a^n)\mapsto xm/b^n$; these maps respect restriction. Composing these identifications with the isomorphism of Step 2 yields the asserted isomorphism.
